title: Why Retrying a Failed API Request Can Accidentally Take Down the Entire Internet — Engineering Cheat Sheet
subtitle: Preventing cascading failures via intelligent retry policies and circuit breakers.
summary: Naive retry logic transforms transient failures into distributed denial-of-service (DDoS) attacks against your own infrastructure. This cheat sheet outlines how to implement resilient communication patterns to avoid triggering systemic cascading outages.

key_concepts.name: Retry Storms
key_concepts.detail: Synchronized retry bursts from multiple clients amplify load during recovery, preventing the downstream service from stabilizing and effectively turning a single node failure into a global outage.

key_concepts.name: Exponential Backoff
key_concepts.detail: An algorithmic approach increasing delay between successive retries (e.g., 2^n), preventing instantaneous re-flooding of a struggling service while providing time for downstream backpressure or auto-scaling to resolve.

key_concepts.name: Jitter
key_concepts.detail: The addition of randomness to backoff intervals to break request synchronization, ensuring that retrying clients distribute load over time rather than hammering the server in lock-step cycles.

code_cheatsheet.explanation: Uses native curl retry logic; prevents manual infinite loops in scripts by setting a maximum total timeout and explicit delay.
Implements exponential backoff with 'full jitter' to decorrelate client request timing and minimize the probability of server-side congestion.

best_practices: Never retry without exponential backoff and jitter to avoid thundering herd scenarios.
Implement Circuit Breakers to stop requests entirely when failure thresholds are met, protecting downstream services.
Set absolute maximum retry limits and enforce strict request timeouts at every layer of the network.
Propagate 'Retry-After' headers from servers to intelligently inform clients when they should cease sending traffic.

interview_qa.question: If your service is experiencing a 503 error, why is simply adding more retries a dangerous anti-pattern?
interview_qa.answer: Retrying against a saturated system adds load to an already failing dependency, worsening the bottleneck. Without backoff and circuit breaking, this creates a positive feedback loop that delays recovery and risks triggering a cascading failure across the entire architecture.
